description: Demolition of the existing building and the erection of a mixed-use building to provide commercial use at ground floor and 6 x residential units to the upper floors.
decision_conditions: <p>In the absence of a Unilateral Undertaking or a Section 106 agreement securing appropriate mitigation by restricting future occupiers of the development from obtaining parking permits within the Controlled Parking Zone the proposed development would likely exacerbate existing parking stress and congestion on the surrounding highway network. The application is, therefore, contrary to Policy LP45 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and Policy T6 of the London Plan (2021).</p>

<p>given the absence of a legal agreement securing the financial contribution towards carbon off-setting having been submitted or completed, the proposal would fail to secure&nbsp; financial contribution towards carbon offsetting; resulting in an unacceptable level of carbon dioxide emissions, contrary to policy LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of residential units 02, 03 and 05 failing to provide dual-aspect accommodation, with the outlook being limited solely to the northern elevation, and noise disturbance to future occupiers from neighbouring noise generating uses, would fail to provide acceptable standards of accommodation. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and policy LP17 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</p>

<p>The proposal, by reason of its proximity to an established late-night music venue and the absence of a representative Noise Impact Assessment and design-led mitigation, fails to demonstrate that the new residential use would not result in unreasonable restrictions being placed on the MOTH Club. The proposal is, therefore, contrary to Policy D13 of the London Plan and the NPPF.</p>

<p>The proposed height, massing, and incoherent architectural detailing would result in an overbearing presence that fails to preserve or enhance the setting of the Mare Street Conservation Area. This results in a level of "less than substantial harm" that is not outweighed by the public benefits of the scheme, contrary to the NPPF (2024) London Plan Policies D1, D3, D4 &amp; HC1 &amp; Local Plan policies LP1 &amp; LP3.</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of a lack of provision of affordable housing, would fail to adequately contribute towards the provision of mixed and balanced communities and housing needs in the local area. As such, the development would not be consistent with policies H4 and H5 of the London Plan (2021), policies LP12 and LP13 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and the Hackney S106 Planning Contributions Supplementary Planning Document (2020).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of a lack of step free access and consequent non provision of wheelchair user, accessible or adaptable dwellings, would provide an inaccessible form of housing provision, to the detriment of housing choice and less able bodied users, contrary to London Plan (2021) policy D7 (Accessible Housing), Hackney LP33 policy LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) and the GLA Mayor’s Housing SPG (2016).</p>

<p>The site has a strong possibility of containing remains of archaeological importance and the application is not supported by an archaeological evaluation. As the required surveys have not been undertaken, officers cannot be certain of the significance of any archaeology in the area, and thus cannot assess how the proposed development would affect this significance. As such, the proposed development conflicts with Local Plan Policy LP6, London Plan HC1 of the London Plan 2021; and paragraph 207 of the NPPF.</p>
